Here are three sentences with 15 characters each, incrementally indented:

    The view was breathtakingly beautiful.
    The view was breathtakingly beautiful.
    The view was breathtakingly beautiful.

And here's a screenplay comparing the sky after a grueling hike and the sky outside a gas station in the city:

FADE IN:

EXT. GAS STATION - DAY

We see a rundown gas station in the outskirts of the city. The sign reads "Eddie's Eats" and the building looks like it's been there for decades.

CUT TO:

EXT. SUMMIT - DAY

We see a hiker, JEN (30s), standing at the summit of a mountain, arms raised in triumph. The sky is a brilliant blue, with just a few wispy clouds.

JEN (V.O)
I did it. I finally made it to the top.

CUT TO:

EXT. GAS STATION - DAY

We see the same gas station, but this time it's at sunset. The sky is a dull grey, with a few clouds that look like they've been sat on.

JEN (V.O)
But as I looked out at the view, I realized that the sky outside Eddie's Eats was almost as breathtaking.

CUT TO:

EXT. GAS STATION - DAY

We see a sign that reads "Eddie's Eats: Home of the World's Worst Burgers". Jen looks out at the sky and shrugs.

JEN (V.O)
I mean, it's not exactly the Grand Canyon, but it's a view.

CUT TO:

EXT. SUMMIT - DAY

We see Jen standing at the summit again, looking out at the sky. This time, she's not alone. A group of seagulls are flying overhead, looking at her like she's crazy.

JEN (V.O)
I guess when you've hiked a mountain, you start to appreciate the little things in life.

CUT TO:

EXT. GAS STATION - DAY

We see the same gas station, but this time it's at night. The sign reads "Eddie's Eats: Open 24/7". Jen looks out at the sky and smiles.

JEN (V.O)
And sometimes, the view is just a reminder that even in the worst places, there's still beauty to be found.

FADE OUT.
